initialContact.message: My wife passed away 8 months ago and I've been avoiding dealing with estate planning. I have three children and five grandchildren. I own our house (worth maybe 250k€) and have 58,000€ in savings. I want to make sure when I die, my children inherit smoothly without fighting or huge tax bills. Should I give money to grandchildren now for education? Make a will? I don't know where to start and it's emotional to think about.

problemContext.currentSituation: Widowed senior needing to plan estate distribution, emotionally difficult, avoiding it
problemContext.emotionalState: grieving, overwhelmed, wanting to do right thing, procrastinating

idealAdvice: First: I'm sorry for your loss. Estate planning after losing spouse is emotionally hard.
Taking 8 months to grieve before handling this is completely normal and healthy
Finnish inheritance system basics:
Without will: Estate divided equally among children (Finnish law)
House (250k) + savings (58k) = 308k€ estate ÷ 3 children = ~103k€ each
Inheritance tax in Finland: First 20k€ tax-free, then 7-19% depending on amount
Each child would owe ~8-10k€ in inheritance tax (manageable from 103k€ inheritance)
Important: Your estate is modest enough that taxes won't devastate heirs
Will (testamentti) - should you make one?
Yes IF: You want different distribution than equal three-way split
Yes IF: You have specific items for specific children (sentimental value)
Not urgent IF: You're happy with equal division, children get along
Lifetime gifts to grandchildren:
Pro: See them enjoy money while you're alive, reduce taxable estate
Con: You might need money for care in coming years (you're 70, could live to 90)
Tax: Gifts over 5,000€ per person subject to gift tax (similar to inheritance tax)
Recommendation: Keep 40k€ for your own security (care costs, housing, life)
Could gift 3,000€ to each grandchild now (15k€ total) - under tax limit, meaningful for education
Remaining 43k€ stays with you for next 10-20 years of life
Practical steps:
1. Have family conversation: Tell children your intentions, reduces future conflict
2. Write simple will if you have specific wishes (lawyer 500-800€)
3. Consider modest gifts to grandchildren if you want to see them benefit
4. Keep majority of assets for YOUR remaining years - you earned this security
You're being thoughtful parent even in grief - your children are lucky
commonMistakes: Not acknowledging grief and emotional difficulty
Overcomplicating Finnish inheritance system (it's fairly straightforward)
Encouraging large gifts without considering his own longevity and care needs
Not mentioning family communication to prevent conflict
Failing to validate that 8 months is normal timeframe to address this
Pushing expensive estate planning when his situation is relatively simple
